tagline.text: The highest peak on Panay, a mossy-forest mountain of clouds and gods

location.label: Location
location.text: Culasi, Antique (Central Panay Mountain Range, bordering Madalag in Aklan)

budget.label: Budget
budget.text: About ₱3,000–8,000 (per person, estimate including transport, guide and food; confirm locally)

children.text: Mount Madja-as rises 2,117 m, making it the highest peak on Panay. Its mossy summit forest, sea of clouds, waterfalls and mythology make it one of the toughest trekking mountains in the Visayas.
Mount Madja-as sits in the city of Culasi in Antique, on the west side of Panay, and is the highest point of the Central Panay Mountain Range. According to Wikipedia it stands about

(6,946 ft) above sea level, making it the highest peak on Panay and, within the Visayas, second only to Mount Kanlaon on Negros. It is classed as a dormant volcano, and the date of its last eruption is unknown. On clear days its outline can be seen to the southwest from Kalibo in Aklan, about
76 km
to the north.

The mountain is as famous for its stories as for its terrain. Ancient Visayans are said to have held it sacred, and its name comes from the Madja-as confederation that is believed to have existed on Panay after the 11th century. In myth, Sidapa, god of death and war, lives on the mountain and measures the lifespan of mortals against a sacred tree; Bulalakaw (god of meteors), Kanlaon (the supreme goddess) and Pandaki (god of second chances) are also linked to it. Hiking here therefore means following old tales as well as a trail.

The natural environment is rich. The summit area is covered in mossy forest, and the so-called crown shyness forest, where treetops leave gaps between each other, and the sea of clouds lying below you have made the mountain famous in photos. The slopes hold 14 waterfalls, and you will notice pitcher plants, orchids and pine trees. The mountain is also the source of four major rivers in northern Antique (the Dalanas, Tibiao, Bacong and Mali-ao) as well as tributaries of the Timbaban and Dumarayray rivers in Aklan, so it supplies water to much of northwestern Panay.

For travelers this is not a casual outing. Wikipedia names the Flores Trail and the Alojipan Trail, both in Culasi, as the easiest routes, says a summit hike usually takes 2 to 3 days, and describes the peak as one of the hardest in the Visayas, alongside Mount Baloy, Mount Nangtud and Mount Kanlaon. The Panipiason Trail on the east face, in Madalag, Aklan, is said to be the most technically difficult. Visitor numbers grew after the mountain went viral on social media in February 2021, so this guide focuses on the geography, gear and local checks you need when planning a climb.

blocks.title: Mossy forest and crown shyness forest

children.text: The higher you climb, the more the trees and rocks are covered in thick moss. The forest where gaps appear between the branches, known as crown shyness, is presented as a symbol of the mountain. Foggy days feel mystical but the trail gets slippery.

When clouds fill the valleys at dawn, a sea of clouds spreads out below you. You need to be on the ridge before sunrise, so camping or a very early start is required. Clouds depend on the weather and are never guaranteed.
The slopes are said to hold 14 waterfalls. Not all are easy to reach, and many stretches of the hike follow the sound of streams. Ask your guide about waterfall locations and access routes.
The upland forest has pitcher plants, orchids and pine trees. The rule is to look only: do not pick or dig up plants. When taking photos, do not step off the trail and trample the vegetation.

This is a mountain with stories of Sidapa, god of death, and the goddess Kanlaon. Before climbing, ask village elders or your guide about the old tales and taboos to enrich your trip. Respect local customs and mountain etiquette.

The Flores and Alojipan trails in Culasi are considered the easier routes, while the Panipiason Trail in Madalag, Aklan, is known as the hardest. On any route a guide is practically mandatory, so check at the trailhead village.

You do not have to reach the foot of the mountain to see it: on clear days it appears on the southwest skyline from Kalibo. Looking for its outline on the way to Boracay through Kalibo is a small pleasure.
Start at the
Culasi municipal tourism office
and confirm whether your date is open, where to start in Flores and how to register, get briefed and obtain a guide. Ask whether a separate police-station log is still required.
Start early and climb along forest paths and streams to the first campsite. Ask your guide where to get food and drinking water.
Start before dawn, pass through the mossy forest and climb to the summit. In good weather you can see the sea of clouds and the sunrise.
After time at the summit, descend and return to the campsite, or continue down to another campsite.
Descend, check out at the village, and travel to Culasi or Kalibo. If rain swells the rivers the descent may be delayed, so keep a spare day.

Section times, campsites and registration methods change with the season and the trail. The schedule above is only an example to help you understand the trip, so always confirm the latest information with a local guide.
Leave your Kalibo hotel toward Culasi. The distance is long, so arrange transport beforehand.
Have lunch in Culasi town and ask the tourism office about the mountain and waterfalls.
Look up at the foothills from the nearby coast or village roads, take photos and head back.
If a summit climb feels like too much, you can plan just a day looking up at the mountain from around Culasi. Adding Mararison Island, just off Culasi, to the day works well.
There are direct flights from Manila to Kalibo International Airport (KLO), taking about
1 hour
. Schedules change by season, so check when booking.
You can also fly from Manila to Iloilo Airport (ILO) and travel overland up toward Antique. From either city the final stretch to Culasi is by road.
Airlines and routes change often, so check the latest information.
According to Wikipedia, Culasi is about
90 km
south of Kalibo, the capital of Aklan, and about
92 km
north of San Jose de Buenavista, the capital of Antique.
At Kalibo terminal, the
Ceres guide lists Mohon buses via Antique
. Verify the Culasi stop and actual fare before boarding. Local operators also publish private vehicle rates by class, separate from bus fares.
The Flores trail starts in Barangay Flores. A
2019 climb report
paid
one way per motorcycle from Culasi to Flores. A 2026 report also used motorcycles. Arrange the return pickup and allow for rough road sections.
Unpaved sections are slippery after rain, so allow extra time and agree the schedule with your driver in advance.
The
Flores Trail guide

describes registration and orientation at Culasi’s tourism office, then a logbook entry at the police station. Ask the office about current requirements and whether your route starts at Flores or exits at Alojipan.
The Panipiason Trail from the Madalag side to the east is known as the most technically difficult and is not recommended unless you are an experienced mountaineer.
If you want to use this trail, check with the Madalag local government and a guide, and do not hike alone.
The safest time for Mount Madja-as is the dry season, December to May. In the rainy season rivers rise and trails turn slippery, making accidents far more likely, so it is wiser to postpone.

Even in the dry season the summit is often wrapped in cloud and fog, and temperatures swing widely. A pre-dawn start is needed for the sea of clouds and sunrise, and the weather cannot be known until the last moment, so keep a spare day. Whether climbing is allowed can change with weather and local government guidance.

There are no restaurants on the mountain, so you must prepare your own food. Bring rice, canned food, instant noodles, energy bars, nuts and electrolyte drinks, and agree in advance whether your guide will cook. In the villages you can try local dishes such as grilled fish with rice and coconut-based food, and around Kalibo there are many more ordinary restaurants. Carry all your trash back down. After the climb, recover with hot soup dishes and fresh fruit at a restaurant in Culasi or Kalibo. Choose boiled or bottled water in the villages, and bring medicine for an upset stomach.
Tell the
Culasi municipal tourism office
whether you will return via Flores or descend through Alojipan. Confirm guide and porter rates and registration requirements.
Bring a waterproof jacket, spare socks and a waterproof bag. The summit is cool even by day and things get wet easily.
Be sure to pack a headlamp, power bank, whistle, first-aid kit and emergency food.
Tell your hotel or family your hiking schedule and contact details before you leave.
Phone signal on the mountain may be almost nonexistent, so download offline maps.
Do not take plants or stones, and follow your guide's instructions when lighting fires at campsites.
Respect village customs and the rules of sacred places, and do not make loud noise or leave trash.
Build fitness for a few weeks beforehand with stair climbing and long walks.
Wear broken-in waterproof hiking boots; avoid new shoes, which cause blisters. Trekking poles ease the strain on your knees on steep descents.
Bring plenty of cash. ATMs are rare outside Culasi, and guide fees are usually paid in cash.
It is counted among the hardest mountains in the Visayas, and a hiker is said to have gone missing on a descent in the past. Never climb alone; always go with a local guide.
In the rainy season rivers can rise suddenly and cut the trail. Postpone your plans if it rains.
The summit is thick with fog and has few trail markers, so it is easy to get lost.
Carry enough clothing and water to guard against hypothermia and dehydration.
Whether climbing is allowed and the entry rules can change with local circumstances, so check the latest notice with the Culasi tourism office just before you leave.
Rescue can take a long time in an emergency, so check your insurance and your emergency contact plan.
A small island just off Culasi, good for relaxing by the sea before or after the climb.
A town in northern Antique known for its river, waterfalls and rapids, a good add-on to a trip around the foot of the mountain.
The capital of Aklan and the gateway city on the way to the mountain. On clear days the mountain can be seen to the southwest.
The leading beach resort close to Kalibo, ideal for resting after a climb.
